scope: 5 static action key poses for each of P1 and P2; not animated clips

actions.label: 걷기
actions.definition: A single controlled key pose of a relaxed four-beat WALK, not running, jumping or begging. Dog travels toward image-left in a readable three-quarter side view. Body supported horizontally above ground at normal standing height; one near forepaw is lifted and reaching forward with a natural slightly bent elbow, the other forepaw is bearing weight; hind paws make a plausible staggered step. Show exactly four anatomical limbs total, far limbs can partially overlap but no duplicate paws. Head at ordinary walking height, face angled slightly toward camera so both small round dot eyes can be seen. Tail follows its reference design naturally; no new tail shape. Tiny friendly mouth may remain, no added excitement symbols.

actions.label: 엎드려 쉬기
actions.definition: A clear awake STERNAL LYING REST pose, not sitting, not side sleeping. Chest and abdomen resting low on the ground; BOTH forelegs extend forward parallel with two small forepaws visible and evenly supported. Hind legs folded naturally underneath or beside the same side of the body, no human knees or extra paws. Head gently raised and looking toward viewer, both UPDATED small round dot eyes open. Mouth softly closed if needed for a calm rest; this is not a claim of sleep or trust. Three-quarter front-side view, whole low horizontal body and tail visible.

actions.label: 앞발 하나 들기
actions.definition: A seated ONE-FOREPAW HOVER pose. Hindquarters stay seated and supported; ONE front paw nearest the camera is lifted only to lower chest level with elbow and wrist softly bent, hovering freely with no object or hand to touch. The OTHER forepaw is clearly planted on the ground and bears weight. Two hind limbs remain naturally folded and support the seated dog. Not standing on two legs, not waving with a human arm, not pawing another object. Show paw as a small dog paw, not a hand or exposed human-like palm. Head stays level and both updated small round dot eyes visible. Choice of visible paw is an illustration choice, not inferred left/right habit.

actions.label: 기지개
actions.definition: A readable FRONT-BODY STRETCH key pose: both forepaws planted farther forward, forelegs extended diagonally forward, chest lowered close to floor while hindquarters/hips stay visibly HIGH on the two standing hind legs. Elongate the pose through normal joints, not by stretching the actual torso or neck length. Spine forms one continuous natural slope from raised hips to low shoulders. Head follows low shoulder level, angled enough toward camera that small round dot eyes remain visible; keep muzzle from touching ground. Side three-quarter view. Four limbs total and all contact points plausible, hind paws behind hips, no collapsing hindquarters. This isolated pose can resemble a play bow; do not add toys/play emotion or assert either behavioral context.

actions.label: 몸 털기
actions.definition: One legible MID-SHAKE key pose of a brief WHOLE-BODY SHAKE, not trembling/shivering. Dog is standing on ALL FOUR PAWS, grounded and spaced for balance. Torso makes a small plausible axial twist, head turns slightly to one side, short floppy ears and cheek/tail fur flick outward with the motion. Keep exactly ONE crisp head, ONE body and ONE tail, do not duplicate silhouettes or smear facial features. Show both updated small ROUND DOT eyes clearly; no spirals, closed X eyes, dizziness or distress symbols. Add at most two or three small curved charcoal motion ticks near ear and flank to suggest the oscillation. No water droplets, no bath props, no floating paws, no exaggerated contortion or rubber body. Recognizability and gentle anatomy take priority over dramatic movement.

instruction_provenance: Action labels and distinctions derive from existing research. Exact limb placement, gaze and composition are illustrative production instructions, not verbatim scientific findings or observed individual habits.
comparison_limit: Both bases received identical action instructions. This does not isolate the benefit of motion instructions versus no motion instructions.
